gaps.why_now: The shared Phase 12 build gate now runs the landed nvme PCI starter beside the phase12 surveys so the complex-driver lane stays reviewable in one bounded path.

The shared Phase 12 make target now runs the nvme PCI starter beside the survey gates for the tranche's other complex-driver lanes, which keeps this survey checkpoint reviewable through one bounded entry point.

The first bounded starter is now landed around a lab-only queue planner that validates queue geometry, computes DMA page demand, assigns monotonic queue identifiers, derives doorbell offsets, records one bounded doorbell-window summary, derives PRP buffer-shape and PRP metadata summaries, and keeps all of that reviewable without claiming live PCI behavior.

Dedicated driver tests now keep the starter honest around admin and I/O queue planning, DMA page rounding, invalid geometry rejection, reset-time queue freeze behavior, the queue-recovery replay helper, the PRP buffer-shape helper, the PRP metadata helper, the doorbell-window helper, and one tiny PRP-versus-SGL selection summary.

The slice note records what the landed queue planner, doorbell-window helper, queue-recovery replay helper, PRP buffer-shape helper, PRP metadata helper, and pointer-selection helper cover so the survey can focus on the remaining roadmap gap instead of re-explaining the starter surface.

The landed virtio_net probe snapshot starter now gives the broader Phase 12 tranche a second real complex-driver foothold, which helps compare the nvme PCI lane against another bounded driver starter instead of only against survey scaffolding.

The landed virtio_scsi queue-layout starter gives the Phase 12 tranche a third real complex-driver foothold, which makes the nvme PCI survey more honest about current peer progress and keeps future runs from treating nvme as the only driver with a starter.
A dedicated survey gate is the smallest truthful way to record that the nvme PCI starter has landed while the deeper transport and DMA roadmap work remains intentionally incomplete.

The lane needs an archival note and pinned raw-read fallback map that compare the current starter against the roadmap so future runs do not mistake the bounded queue, recovery, doorbell-window, and data-pointer planning slice for a production PCI port or borrow another lane's fallback catalog.

The landed PRP buffer-shape helper now records first-page offset, rounded span, and page-list bound checks without crossing into SGL setup, live DMA mapping, request submission, or hardware-backed queue setup.

The landed doorbell-window helper now summarizes the bounded SQ/CQ register aperture across the admin queue and already-planned I/O queue pairs, including reset visibility, without claiming live MMIO access, MSI-X vector wiring, or hardware-backed queue creation.

The landed queue-recovery replay helper now summarizes capped I/O queue replay, preserved admin geometry, aggregate host DMA demand, and reset-frozen visibility after reset without claiming live PCI queue recreation, MMIO access, or IRQ-backed completion flow.

The landed pointer-selection helper now records the bounded PRP-versus-SGL decision surface around admin-versus-I/O queues, page-gap forcing, user-command forcing, integrity-segment forcing, and average-segment threshold preference without claiming live descriptor allocation or DMA mapping.

Host Memory Buffer management, blk-mq queue_rq paths, live PCI queue creation, IRQ-driven completion polling, timeout recovery plumbing, and real PRP or SGL DMA mapping remain blocked even though the smaller queue planner, queue-recovery replay helper, doorbell-window helper, PRP buffer-shape helper, PRP metadata helper, and pointer-selection helper are now landed and the roadmap-approved DMA-safe transport substrate is still missing.
